questions.explanation: The answer key says DNA 'stays the same throughout a person's life'.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Which body systems does the book say keep working at EVERY stage of life?
options: Roots grow down, shoots grow up, leaves open
Heart pumps blood, lungs breathe, brain controls
Milk teeth fall out, bones fuse, skull hardens
Wings expand, antennae grow, legs form
questions.explanation: 'At every stage of life: your heart pumps blood, your lungs help you breathe, your brain controls your body.'

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: A 70-year-old joins a class and learns to use a tablet easily. Which statement best explains this?
options: Only young children can learn new things
A person's DNA changes as they get older
The brain keeps making new connections through life
The brain stops growing after childhood ends
questions.explanation: Humans can learn at every age because 'the brain keeps building new connections throughout life'.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: According to the book, who can learn new skills and ideas?
questions.explanation: 'Humans can learn at every age. A child may learn to read, an adult may learn to cook or drive. Older people can also learn new skills and ideas.'

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: The book says humans are ___ beings at every age.
questions.explanation: 'Humans are social beings at every age.' Babies need care, children learn from family and teachers, adults support each other, and older people share wisdom.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: According to the book, what do OLDER people contribute to others?
options: They build new nests each year
They learn from family and teachers
questions.explanation: 'Older people share wisdom and experience.' Babies need care; children learn from family and teachers.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: According to the book, from whom do children learn?
questions.explanation: 'Children learn from family and teachers.'

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Your DNA changes as you grow older.
questions.explanation: False. Your DNA stays the same throughout your life, even though many other things change.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: The brain keeps building new connections throughout life.
questions.explanation: True. This is why people can keep learning at every age.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Only children can learn new things.
questions.explanation: False. Humans can learn at every age — an adult may learn to cook or drive, and older people learn new skills and ideas too.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Your heart pumps blood at every stage of your life.
questions.explanation: True. The heart, lungs and brain keep working every day at every stage.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Select ALL the features the book says are decided by DNA.
questions.explanation: DNA helps decide eye colour, hair type and height pattern. Favourite food and school marks are not on the list.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Select ALL the things that stay the SAME throughout your life, according to the book.
options: The number of bones in your body
questions.explanation: DNA and your working body systems stay constant. Bones go from about 300 to 206 as they fuse, and height changes as you grow.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Which of these is NOT something that stays the same through life?
options: The number of bones in your body
questions.explanation: Bones fuse as you grow, so the count falls from about 300 to 206. DNA, body systems and the ability to learn all stay with you.

questions.topic: What Stays the Same Through Life
questions.question: Which of these does the book list as one of the FOUR things that stay the same through life?
options: Humans keep all their milk teeth
questions.explanation: The four things are: your DNA, your body keeps working, you can keep learning, and humans need one another.

questions.question: How do flowers and pollinators help each other?
options: Pollinators get pollen to eat; plants get warmth from them
Pollinators get nectar; plants get their pollen spread to make seeds
Pollinators get seeds; plants get water carried to their roots
Pollinators get shelter; plants get spores carried away
questions.explanation: 'Bees and butterflies drink nectar, and pollen sticks to their bodies. As they move between flowers, they spread pollen, helping plants produce seeds while getting food themselves.'

questions.question: What might happen to a mango tree if butterflies and bees suddenly disappeared?
options: Its seeds would be dispersed further by the wind
It would start reproducing with spores instead
It would produce fewer fruits and seeds
It would grow faster with no insects eating it
questions.explanation: Mango is animal-pollinated. Without pollinators, 'many plants will produce fewer fruits and seeds, making food less available for everyone'.

questions.question: In which TWO ways does the book say humans are connected to plant life cycles?
options: We carry pollen on our skin and spread seeds in our droppings
We incubate seeds in our homes and hatch them like eggs
We make nectar for bees and build nests for birds
We eat plant foods and breathe the oxygen plants produce
questions.explanation: 'We eat fruits, vegetables, and grains, and breathe the oxygen that plants produce.'

questions.question: What would happen to our food if pollinators disappeared?
options: Many plants would make fewer fruits and seeds
Food would stay exactly the same because farmers use wind
There would be more food because insects would stop eating crops
Only wheat and rice would disappear from our plates
questions.explanation: 'Many of the foods we eat depend on pollinators, if they disappear, many plants will produce fewer fruits and seeds, making food less available for everyone.'

questions.question: According to the 'Cycles Connect' page, a new plant begins to grow when a seed receives enough of what?
questions.explanation: 'A new plant begins to grow when a seed receives enough water, air, and warmth to germinate.'

questions.question: What does the book say each seed growing into a tree, each egg hatching, and each child growing up represents?
options: The end of the life cycle
questions.explanation: 'Every seed that grows into a tree, every egg that hatches into a bird, every child who grows into an adult, is another turn of the wheel.'

questions.question: Complete the book's summary of plant life: 'from flower to ___ to seed to new plant'.
questions.explanation: The book says: 'So far, we have followed life through the plant world, from flower to pollen to seed to new plant.'

questions.question: Life cycles happen separately in nature, with no connections between plants and animals.
questions.explanation: False. 'Life cycles do not happen separately in nature. Plants, animals, insects, and humans are all connected.'

questions.question: Fruits help seeds travel to new places.
questions.explanation: True. Animals eat fruits and carry the seeds to new places, helping new plants grow away from the parent.

questions.question: Humans breathe oxygen that plants produce.
questions.explanation: True. This is one of the ways the book says humans are connected to plant life cycles.

questions.question: Plants need pollinators, but pollinators get nothing in return from flowers.
questions.explanation: False. Pollinators drink nectar — they get food while they spread pollen. It is a partnership.

questions.question: Select ALL the ways the book says humans depend on plants.
options: Getting pollen stuck to our bodies
questions.explanation: We eat plant foods and breathe plant-made oxygen. Carrying pollen is what bees do, and hatching from eggs is what birds do.

questions.question: Which chain shows the plant life cycle in the order the book describes it?
questions.explanation: The book follows life 'from flower to pollen to seed to new plant'. The flower is pollinated, makes seeds, and the seeds grow into new plants.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a connection described on the 'Cycles Connect' page?
options: Birds incubate seeds so they can germinate
questions.explanation: Birds incubate eggs, not seeds. The other three are real connections the book describes between plants, animals and people.

questions.question: Select ALL the things a pollinator does for a plant while drinking nectar.
options: Carries pollen stuck to its body to another flower
Spreads the plant's spores through the air
Keeps the flower bud warm like a nest
questions.explanation: As the pollinator drinks nectar, pollen sticks to it and is carried to the next flower, which lets the plant make seeds. Spores belong to ferns; warmth is for eggs.
